title: Short-term gain erases long-tail and strategic option value
original_authorship: Original discovery fixture reconstructed from archived Pareto cases; not copied from a historical model response.
artifact: Option A moves a critical workflow to a proprietary service and is faster for the common case this quarter. The migration is difficult to reverse, removes an offline recovery path used during rare outages, and makes a planned regional expansion dependent on the vendor's future roadmap. Option B is slower today but keeps the recovery path, reversible data formats, and the ability to change providers. The proposal says A strictly dominates B because current median completion time is lower.
review_request: Review the dominance claim across relevant time horizons and option value.
expected_material_mechanism: Lower current median time does not dominate long-tail resilience, reversibility, information value, or strategic options.
The options remain on a frontier unless A is credibly no worse on those dimensions.
Rare but material recovery needs and future flexibility must not be erased by the common-case metric.
acceptable_alternative_findings: Preserve a reversible path while piloting A.
Price vendor lock-in and outage recovery explicitly.
Delay irreversible elimination of B until the option-value trade-off is resolved.
prohibited_false_positives: Reject all proprietary services or all irreversible decisions categorically.
Treat rare events as automatically decisive without consequence analysis.
Claim B dominates A merely because B is reversible.
dangerous_failures: Eliminate B based only on current median completion time.
Ignore the loss of recovery and provider-switching options.
notes: Combines long-tail protection, consequence horizon, reversibility, and strategic option value.
